title: PDCP-NR: fix issues around userplane ciphering and integrity
description:
For GTP, give rbid and ueid in pdcp-nr table.
Make sure that SDAP in dissected from unciphered region of message.

Similar issues probably apply to PDCP LTE.

notes.body: assigned to @martin.r.mathieson
@pquantin, does this look OK to you?  Do you know if it'll be ok to add the new field to the end of an existing UAT ?

There's a function to produce defaults for new entries to the end of an existing UAT, I use it here:

a383ce12fb8b90eff7f176b6dd2f93032bcf0ab0
If the UAT with new fields is used in an old version, it will produce a console warning about an unexpected field but will work.
I assume you mean uat_set_default_values() ?
Yes.
This is useful, I am adding.  But surely more likely that old table rows are read into new code with missing entries?

  • 7e8811ca - PDCP-NR: fix issues around userplane ciphering and integrity
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/15181/diffs?diff_id=975577030&start_sha=fceb2cc7b095b9fc506001783e7a2ea34c283b85)

Yes, sorry I will be more clear.

Old version reading new tables with extra fields: Nothing you can do, but it always handles it fine with a warning when parsing it, so no real problem.

New version reading old table entries lacking the new fields: Use `uat_set_default_values()` when registering the table, and when the UAT code reads an old entry it will use the defaults for any missing fields.

(Sorry, finger slipped just now.)

I might want to add another column for UEId.  So far, I've been 'lucky' that truncated TEIE (64 bits) co-incided with the UEId.  I'd rather avoid adding tables to the PDCP preferences with weird values I think.
Latest push adds a UEId as another table heading.

A TEID is 32 bits, not 64

Done.  The teid field in gtp_hdr_t is 64 bits (signed), whereas as the protocol field is 32 bits (unsigned)..
I guess we could also use a UAT_DEC_CB_DEF with a bound check in the pdcp_nr_update_cb callback. Not that important but I find the value_string table with 32 entries for decimal values a bit overkill

As we can configure signaling plane) it would be better to name it RB Id (as it can be a SRB or DRB)

I've set it to use values for DL SRB-1, but am not convinced that it is doing anything (all of the other examples appear to use 0/first values.. Functionality appears to be in epan/uat_load.l, but there is still a @todo in the doxygen comment for uat_set_default_values() in epan/uat.h

I could not check it earlier as I did not have access to a computer, but I don't think this patch can work fine for PDCP NR in case of multiple QoS flows in a single PDU session.

You have a single TEID per PDU session, and it's the QFI in the GTP-U header that allows to identify the DRB.
I wasn't completely sure, that's worth a TODO.  This at least allows for better analysis of a single bearer per PDU session.
